description: Lidar-derived digital surface model of Stromboli island updated to August 2023 is a data set described in a peer-reviewed Scientific Data article written by Marina Bisson et al. Digital surface models reproduce the 3D topography of a territory at different spatial resolutions depending on the acquisition technique of source data. In active and densely populated volcanic areas, updated digital topographies are fundamental for mapping and quantifying the morphological changes generated by the eruptive events and are used to model volcanic phenomena and related hazards. Coverage: not stated; published in 2025. Formats: GeoTIFF, Point cloud. The data are held in INGV and reached through its DOI listed on this page; the paper's Data Records section names it. Size stated by the repository: 365 Mbyte. Access is free of charge and open according to the article. The licence is Open Access, taken from DataCite rights of the deposit. Caveats: written from the Scientific Data article metadata (title, abstract, Data Records section) read on 2026-10-01; the data themselves were not opened or downloaded, so their contents, quality and current availability were not checked, and the coverage and resolution are those of the abstract only. It can support multi-sector infrastructure risk and planning studies. Related records: none catalogued yet.
